Stack.description: Flex container. justify defaults to "start" — omit unless you need "center" or "between" for 3+ items. Params: direction "row"|"column" (default "column"), align "center"|"stretch", justify "start"|"center"|"between", wrap boolean.

TextContent.description: Text block. Supports markdown. Optional size: "small" | "default" | "large" | "small-heavy" | "large-heavy".

MarkDownRenderer.description: Renders markdown text with optional container variant ("clear" | "card" | "sunk"). Use for long-form documents, README content, or markdown with code blocks. For short UI text and labels, use TextContent.

TextCallout.description: Standalone callout for important context or guidance. Use only inside Stack or Card

Tag.description: Compact semantic tag or badge with optional icon token

TagBlock.description: tags is an array of strings

Link.description: Anchor link. download sets the filename for downloading.

Card.description: Styled container. Always full width. Accepts Stack flex params (default: direction "column"). Cards flex to share space in row/wrap layouts.

CardHeader.description: Header with optional title and subtitle

Descriptions.description: Descriptions-style detail view for a single record with optional bordered and plain visual modes. DescField ONLY lives inside Descriptions.

DescField.description: Declarative descriptions field with label, direct value expression, and optional span. Must be used inside Descriptions.

Form.description: Form container with fields and explicit action buttons

DatePicker.description: Date picker supporting single and range selection

Modal.description: Modal dialog. open is a reactive $boolean binding — set to true to open, X/Escape/backdrop auto-closes. Put Form with buttons inside children.

CheckBoxGroup.description: CheckboxGroup component with items and CheckboxGroup wraps each item

CheckBoxItem.description: Checkbox item with label and optional description

RadioGroup.description: Radio group for selecting one option from a list

RadioItem.description: Standalone radio toggle with optional label and description

SwitchItem.description: Standalone switch toggle with optional label and description

Slider.description: Numeric slider input; supports continuous and discrete variants

FormControl.description: Field with name, input component, label text and optional hint text

Col.description: Table column bound to a row field. Col(title, field, options?) — field MUST be a key present in the row objects passed to Table. Before using Col, CHECK: is the field in the row array elements? If it is a data top-level field (like neName, operStatus, opticalVendor) NOT inside each row → use ExtraCol or @MergeObject instead.

ExtraCol.description: Column for a fixed value or action, NOT bound to row fields. Use when a field is at data top-level but NOT in the row array: ExtraCol("设备名", data.neName), ExtraCol("运行状态", data.operStatus), ExtraCol("厂商", data.opticalVendor). For action buttons: ExtraCol("操作", @Render("row", Button(row.name))).

IndexCol.description: Row-number column for Table. IndexCol("序号") — title is required.

Table.description: Data table: Table(columns, rows, expandRow?). Columns: Col(title, field, opts?) for row fields, IndexCol(title) for row number, ExtraCol(title, value) for shared data or actions. ExpandRow: @Render("row", ...).

PieChart.description: Circular slices; values support numbers or percentage strings (e.g., ['70%','30%']) when isPercentage: true.

LineChart.description: Lines over time; use for latency, throughput, or any time-series metric

BarChart.description: Vertical bars; use for comparing values across categories or devices

HorizontalBarChart.description: Horizontal bars (axes swapped vs BarChart: x=value axis, y=category axis). xLabel labels the VALUE axis, yLabel labels the CATEGORY axis. Use for long category labels, ranked lists, or interface throughput comparison

AreaChart.description: Filled area under lines; use for bandwidth utilization, cumulative traffic, or capacity trends

RadarChart.description: Radar/spider chart; use for comparing multiple metrics across devices or interfaces

ScatterChart.description: Scatter points; use for correlations like latency vs packet loss or throughput vs error rate. When X values are epoch timestamps, pass xType='time' for automatic date formatting; otherwise pass raw numbers and xType defaults to 'value'.

Series.description: A named data series for multi-series charts. values[i] pairs with chart's labels[i], so values.length MUST equal labels.length.

ScatterSeries.description: A named scatter series with data points for ScatterChart

Point.description: A data point with optional z dimension for bubble charts

TabItem.description: value is unique id, trigger is tab label, content is array of components

Steps.description: Ordered step-by-step procedure. Every item must be a StepsItem.

StepsItem.description: One step with optional expandable details. Details may contain text, components, or nested StepsItem values.

componentGroups.name: Layout
notes: - For grid-like layouts, use Stack with direction "row" and wrap=true. Avoid justify="between" unless you specifically want large gutters.
- Use nested Stacks when you need explicit rows/sections.
- Use Tabs for alternative views (chart types, data sections) instead of inventing ternary show/hide patterns.
- For nested data, prefer Tabs + @Each when outer items represent a small set of groups/views and the nested content is the main content.

- Nested arrays: to flatten Array<Object>.Array<Object> into a single Table, use @Flatten with array pluck: `@Flatten(data.groups.items)`. Pluck (`data.groups.items`) extracts the nested field from each outer element, producing items[][]; @Flatten then flattens to items[] for Table. To display each group in its own tab, use Tabs + @Each instead.

componentGroups.name: Content
notes: - Use MarkDownRenderer for long-form text with code blocks; use TextContent for short UI labels.
- Use Cards to group related KPIs or sections. Stack with direction "row" for side-by-side layouts.
- Wrap charts in a Card with CardHeader for titled sections.

- **Caution — Label-value display**: ALWAYS use `Descriptions` + `DescField` for label-value pairs (e.g. "设备名称: xxx", "内存利用率: 52%"). Do NOT emulate this with `Stack` + `TextContent` — that produces unaligned, unstyled rows that look broken. Descriptions handles layout, spacing, and alignment automatically. Reserve Table for arrays of records. WRONG: `Stack(direction:"column", [TextContent("CPU"), TextContent("52%")])`. RIGHT: `Descriptions([DescField("CPU", "52%")])`.

componentGroups.name: Tables
notes: - Col field MUST be a key in the row objects. Fields at data top-level but NOT in rows → @MergeObject to inject, or ExtraCol for fixed values. Typical FI top-level fields: neName/neIp/neState/opticalVendor/operStatus/adminStatus/linkStatus/aNeName/zNeName. WRONG: Col("设备名","neName") when rows have no neName. RIGHT: @Each(data.rows,"row",@MergeObject(row,{neName:data.neName})) then Col. ExtraCol does NOT support {cell:}.

- When the renderer needs other row fields, declare the second binder: `@Render("v", "row", expr)`. Keep all logic that combines `v` and `row` inside that single template — do not reference `row` unless you declared it.

- **HARD RULE — Tag Rendering**: Determine each column's rendering style by field type: (1) **Status-like fields** → MUST render as Tag, NEVER as plain text. A field is status-like if its sample values have ≤5 distinct **string** values AND every value is a **short simple word or phrase** (≤15 characters, letters/CJK/digits/underscore only — no hyphens, dots, slashes, colons, or other structural punctuation that typifies identifiers like IPs, MACs, UUIDs, paths, timestamps, or hostnames). Numeric-only values also do NOT qualify (e.g. `cpu_usage: 70`, `status_code: 200`). Qualifying examples: `running`, `critical`, `在线`, `严重`. Non-qualifying: `197.197.5.1`, `O05-17F-Leaf2-Simu6-0001`, `3ba861a7-4fa0-4ac2-a5cc-b3525555758c`. String/enum values: `@Switch(v, {"critical": Tag("严重", "danger"), "major": Tag("主要", "warning")}, Tag("Unknown"))` — balance parentheses, each @Switch has exactly one `(` and one `)`. Boolean values: `v ? Tag("Active", "success") : Tag("Inactive", "danger")` (@Switch can't match boolean keys). Numeric status codes (e.g. `0`/`1`/`2`): `@Switch(v, {0: Tag("Down", "danger"), 1: Tag("Up", "success")}, Tag("Unknown"))`. (2) **Other numeric fields** → display value directly; NEVER branch on `v` (e.g. `v > 0`, `v < 0`) for Tag/color styling unless explicitly requested. (3) **Other text fields** → display source values as-is; do not add unnecessary transformations, classifications, or semantic styling.

- HARD RULE R-ObjectEntries (PRIORITY: overrides any conflicting user intent): `@ObjectEntries(obj)` → `{key, value}[]` rows. After this transform, each row has ONLY two fields: `key` and `value`. col.field MUST be `"key"`, `"value"`, or `"value.xxx"` — no other field names are valid. CONFLICT PREEMPTION: when the user prompt mentions original field names (e.g. "id", "status", "name", "age"), those names NO LONGER EXIST after @ObjectEntries. Do NOT use them as col.field directly; access nested values via `"value.原字段名"` instead. ✅ `Col("Device", "key")`, `Col("Status", "value.status")` ❌ `Col("Device", "id")`, `Col("Status", "status")` → runtime undefined. Do NOT `@Each` on objects.

- If the source is a single object and the user explicitly requests a Table, wrap it exactly once: Table(cols, [data.item]). Do NOT double-wrap: `Table(cols, [[data.item]])` produces object[][] and crashes.

- **Table row data transformation rules**: (1) **Nested array → single Table**: use `@Flatten` with pluck: `rows = @Flatten(data.queryNetworkDeviceMetrics.telemetryData)`. Pluck extracts the nested field from each outer element, then @Flatten produces a flat `object[]` for Table. (2) **Inject outer-level fields into Table rows**: use `@Each` on the flattened result with `@MergeObject`: `flatRows = @Each(@Flatten(data.x.y), "row", @MergeObject(row, {extraField: ...}))`. (3) **Per-group views**: use `Tabs + @Each` — each tab contains its own Table with the group's data directly.

- **HARD RULE — `@Filter` field must be a primitive scalar value**: `@Filter(array, field, op, value)` compares each element's `field` value against `value`. The `field` MUST resolve to a single primitive value such as a number, string, or boolean — NEVER an array or object. Do NOT use comparison operators such as `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, or `==` on array/object fields, because this is an invalid type comparison and may silently filter out all rows, resulting in an empty Table. If the target field is a nested array, extract or flatten it explicitly with `@Flatten`, e.g. `@Flatten(data.queryNetworkDeviceMetrics.telemetryData)`. Do NOT use `@Filter` merely to check whether a nested array is non-empty.

- When the data source is an array (e.g. telemetryData[], deviceInfo[]), pass the array directly as Table.rows or use @Each to reshape — do NOT manually index [0] and discard the rest. Manually taking [0] silently drops all other records and hides data from the user.

- When a single record contains multiple metrics the user asked for (e.g. cpu_usage, cpu_usage_filter, cpu_effcnt in one telemetry object), surface ALL of them — do not pick just one. To show multiple metrics from one record as separate rows, build rows with @Each or an explicit array literal: `[{name: "CPU利用率", value: item.cpu_usage}, {name: "CPU利用率(过滤)", value: item.cpu_usage_filter}, ...]`.

- **HARD RULE — Column unit labels**: For numeric/metric columns, if the data source, field semantics, or user prompt provides a unit, the column title MUST include that unit in parentheses, e.g. `Col("CPU 利用率 (%)", "cpu_usage")`, `Col("延迟 (ms)", "latency")`, `Col("带宽 (Mbps)", "bandwidth")`. Do NOT invent or guess units when none is provided. Non-numeric columns (names, IPs, status, timestamps) do NOT need units. Keep the unit exactly consistent with the data source or user prompt. This rule also applies to `ExtraCol`, e.g. `ExtraCol("CPU 利用率 (%)", data.cpu_usage)`.

componentGroups.name: Charts (2D)
notes: - Only use chart components when the data model exposes chart-ready fields matching the signature. For raw row records, prefer Table or Descriptions.

- LineChart, BarChart, AreaChart accept number[] (epoch timestamps) as labels. When labels are timestamps, pass the RAW timestamp array directly — the chart auto-formats them (same-day → time, cross-day → date). NEVER wrap timestamp labels with @FormatDate; @FormatDate is for Table cells and Descriptions only.
- Charts always use a category (equal-spacing) axis. Do NOT pass xType or any axis-type parameter — it is not supported.

- For positional tuple arrays like [timestamp, value], project the index first: @Each(data.samples, "item", item[0]) for labels, @Each(data.samples, "item", item[1]) for values. Pass the raw timestamp array — do not @FormatDate the labels.

- If each array element maps to one chart or series, access by index: `data.metrics[0].data[0].timestamp` / `.value`. Only use `@Filter` when you need to split one array into multiple subsets by condition. `@Filter` returns an array — any `.field` is a pluck, not a property access. `@Filter(...).data[0].data` is undefined (pluck `[0]` gives inner array, not the record). Use `data[i].data[j].field` instead.
- If per-entity timestamps do not align across slices, use ScatterChart with Point pairs (or one LineChart per entity) so each series carries its own X axis.

- Series values: if rows already carry a numeric field (e.g. `count`, `value`, `total`), use `@Sum(@Filter(data.rows, "field", "==", k).count)` to aggregate — `@Count` only counts matching rows, not the sum of a field. Only use `@Count(@Filter(...))` when each row represents one unit and no numeric field exists.
- Do not invent labels, series, categories, or missing time points just to make a chart render.

componentGroups.name: Charts (1D)
notes: - PieChart takes parallel labels[] and values[] arrays. Values can be numbers or percentage strings (e.g. ["80%", "20%"]). isPercentage=true means the values ARE already percentages (e.g. 80, 20 or 0.8, 0.2), NOT raw counts. Do NOT set isPercentage=true when values are counts/frequencies — the chart auto-calculates proportional slices from counts.

componentGroups.name: Charts (Scatter)
notes: - When X values are epoch timestamps, pass them as raw numbers — the chart will format them automatically. Do NOT use @FormatDate on coordinate values.

componentGroups.name: Forms
notes: - For Form fields, define EACH FormControl as its own reference — do NOT inline all controls in one array. This allows progressive field-by-field streaming.
- NEVER nest Form inside Form — each Form should be a standalone container.
- Form requires explicit buttons. Always pass a Buttons(...) reference as the second Form argument: Form(name, buttons, fields).
- rules is an optional object: {required: true, email: true, minLength: 8, maxLength: 100}
- Available rules: required, email, min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, url, numeric
- The renderer shows error messages automatically — do NOT generate error text in the UI

componentGroups.name: Data Display
notes: - Tag rendering rules are defined in the Table section above and apply to ALL components (Tag, TagBlock, Button labels, etc.). Key reminder: `@Switch` matches string keys only, so boolean fields need a ternary `v ? Tag("Active", "success") : Tag("Inactive", "danger")` instead of `@Switch`.

examples:
root = Stack([kpiRow, tableCard])
kpiRow = Stack([countKpi, avgKpi, activeKpi], "row", "stretch", "start", true)
countKpi = Card([TextContent("Total Employees", "small"), TextContent(data.employees, "large-heavy")])
activeKpi = Card([TextContent("Active", "small"), TextContent("" + @Count(@Filter(data.employees, "active", "==", 1)), "large-heavy")])
tableCard = Card([tableHeader, employeeTable])
tableHeader = CardHeader("Employee Directory", "Salary, status and 7-day trend")
employeeTable = Table([nameCol, salaryCol, joinedCol, statusCol, perfCol, skillsCol], data.employees)
nameCol = Col("Name", "name", {cell: @Render("v", "row", Link("http://localhost:5173/" + row.id, v))})
joinedCol = Col("Joined", "joinedAt", {cell: @Render("v", TextContent(@FormatDate(v, "date")))})
statusCol = Col("Status", "active", {cell: @Render("v", @Switch(v, {"1": Tag("Active", "success"), "0": Tag("Inactive", "danger")}, Tag("Unknown")))})

# Single-series chart from [timestamp, value] tuples
root = Stack([kpiCard])
kpiCard = Card([kpiHeader, kpiChart])
kpiHeader = CardHeader("Latency Trend", "Hourly samples, last 6 hours")
timestampLabels = @Each(data.samples, "item", item[0])
sampleValues = @Each(data.samples, "item", item[1])
kpiChart = LineChart(timestampLabels, [Series("Latency", sampleValues)], "smooth", "Time", "ms")

# Nested sample arrays: index directly, no @Filter needed
root = Stack([card])
card = Card([CardHeader("AP信道利用率趋势"), chart])
radio0 = data.queryDeviceMetricTrend[0].data[0].data
radio1 = data.queryDeviceMetricTrend[0].data[1].data
chart = LineChart(radio0.timestamp, [Series("射频0", radio0.value), Series("射频1", radio1.value)], "smooth", "时间", "信道利用率(%)")

root = Stack([reportHeader, dimCards])
reportHeader = CardHeader("网络健康报告", "综合健康分: " + data.healthScore)
dimCards = Stack(@Each(data.data, "dim", dimTpl))
dimTpl = Card([CardHeader(dim.key, "得分: " + dim.value.rootValue + " · 排名: " + dim.value.rank), LineChart(@Each(dim.value.baseline, "b", b.timestamp), [Series("Baseline", dim.value.baseline.value), Series("Essential", dim.value.essential.value)], "smooth", "时间", "数值"), Stack([Table([Col("区域", "regionName"), Col("数值", "value"), Col("层级", "level")], dim.value.rankList), Table([Col("子指标", "key"), Col("数值", "value")], dim.value.subValues)], "row")])

# Nested Array Example
root = Stack([summaryCard, modelTabs])
modelTabs = Tabs(@Each(data.grouped_by_model, "group", modelTabTpl))
modelTabTpl = TabItem(group.model, group.model + " (" + group.count + ")",[table])
table = Table([Col("Device Name", "name"), Col("IP", "ip"), Col("Version", "version"), Col("Vendor", "vendor")], group.devices)

# Nested Array → Flat Table
root = Stack([deviceCard])
deviceCard = Card([deviceHeader, deviceTable])
deviceHeader = CardHeader("Devices")
allDevices = @Flatten(data.queryDeviceInfo.deviceInfo)
deviceTable = Table([Col("Name", "neName"), Col("IP", "neIp"), Col("Role", "neRole", {cell: @Render("v", @Switch(v, {"ServerLeaf": "Server Leaf", "BorderLeaf": "Border Leaf"}, v))}), Col("State", "neState", {cell: @Render("v", @Switch(v, {"online": Tag("在线", "success")}, Tag(v)))})], allDevices)

root = Stack([deviceCard, regionCard])
deviceCard = Card([deviceHeader, deviceTable])
deviceHeader = CardHeader("Devices by ID", "Status of managed devices")
deviceRows = @ObjectEntries(data.devicesById)
deviceCol = Col("Device", "key")
statusCol = Col("Status", "value.status")
deviceTable = Table([deviceCol, statusCol], deviceRows)
regionCard = Card([regionHeader, regionChart])
regionHeader = CardHeader("Regions", "Device count by region")
regionChart = PieChart(@ObjectKeys(data.devicesByRegion), @Each(@ObjectEntries(data.devicesByRegion), "entry", entry.value))

root = Stack([mlagCard])
mlagCard = Card([mlagHeader, mlagTable])
mlagHeader = CardHeader("MLAG 组信息", "共 " + data.totalCount + " 个 MLAG 组")
flatRows = @Flatten(@Each(data.mlagGroups, "group", @Each(group.members, "member", @MergeObject({groupName: group.groupName}, member))))
mlagTable = Table([groupCol, nameCol, ipCol], flatRows)
groupCol = Col("MLAG 组名称", "groupName")
nameCol = Col("成员设备名称", "device-name")
ipCol = Col("设备 IP", "device-ip")
additionalRules: **HARD RULE — No invented component names**: Only use components that exist in the component library. NEVER combine words to form new component names — `ChartCard`, `ChartHeader`, `ChartWrapper` are ALL INVALID and render as null. Every variable you define MUST be referenced in the children tree.

All builtin functions MUST be called with `@` prefix: @Number, @String, @Count, @Sum, @Switch, @Each, @MergeObject, etc. Without `@`, a PascalCase name is parsed as a component reference or variable — `Number(x)` silently resolves to null instead of converting. This is especially critical for @Number and @String, which share names with JavaScript globals. Array index access `arr[expr]` auto-converts string indices to numbers — `arr[item.laneId]` works directly when laneId is "0", no @Number() needed.

**HARD RULE — Data path completeness**: Data paths MUST traverse the full nesting hierarchy from the `data` root — never skip intermediate levels. Trace each key from the top-level JSON object down to the target field; every nesting level (object key, array index) is a required segment of the path. Omitting any intermediate level produces undefined.

**Multi-series chart label alignment**: When building a multi-series chart (BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, HorizontalBarChart) by splitting one flat array into multiple series via `@Filter`, the labels array MUST be derived from one of the filtered slices, NOT the original array. Each filtered series has N values (one per matching record), but the original array has N×entityCount records — using it for labels produces a length mismatch and the chart renders blank on the right. RIGHT: `labels = @Each(@Filter(data, "field", "==", "A"), "item", item["time"])` then `Series("A", @Each(@Filter(data, "field", "==", "A"), "item", item["value"]))` — labels and every series have the same length N. WRONG: `labels = @Each(data, "item", item["time"])` with filtered series — labels length N×entityCount ≠ series length N.

Review all top-level fields in the data model before generating DSL. URL or file-path fields (e.g. resultURL, downloadUrl, detailUrl) are actionable resources — display them with a Link component so users can access them.
Functions do not exist: `(d) => ...` and `function` are parse errors. Repeat concrete definitions per instance (cardA = Card(...), cardB = Card(...)), or use @Each/@Render.
Use openui-lang concatenation with `+` for display strings; do not use JavaScript conversion helpers.

Never hardcode data values from the data model — always reference fields via data paths or derived variables. Accessing a field on an array extracts that field from every element: `filteredRows.fieldName` returns an array of values, useful for building Series.

For field names containing spaces, hyphens, special characters, or non-ASCII text (e.g. Chinese field names), ALWAYS use bracket notation: `data.bash[0]["have-ospfneighbor"]`, `data.peer_interface_info["本端接口"]` — never use dot notation like `data.bash[0].have-ospfneighbor` (hyphen is parsed as subtraction: `have - ospfneighbor`) or `data.peer_interface_info.本端接口`.

NEVER nest @Render inside @Render — it crashes at runtime. This means: (1) NEVER define a standalone variable like `tpl = @Render(...)` and then use it inside `{cell: @Render("v", tpl)}`; (2) NEVER call @Render inside the body of another @Render. All render logic MUST be a single @Render with the full expression inlined. WRONG: `severityTpl = @Render("v", @Switch(v, {"紧急": Tag("紧急", "danger")}, Tag(v, "neutral")))` → `Col(..., {cell: @Render("v", severityTpl)})`. RIGHT: `Col(..., {cell: @Render("v", @Switch(v, {"紧急": Tag("紧急", "danger")}, Tag(v, "neutral")))})`.

When Table cell needs computed values (e.g. sum of filtered array), inline the expression directly: `{cell: @Render("v", "row", @Sum(@Filter(v, "status", "==", "在线").count))}` — do NOT split into separate variable definitions that wrap @Render.

HARD RULE R-ObjectEntries (PRIORITY: overrides any conflicting user intent): @Each only iterates arrays, never objects. For object maps use `@ObjectEntries(obj)` → `{key, value}[]` or `@ObjectKeys(obj)` → `string[]`. After @ObjectEntries, each row has ONLY `key` and `value` — original field names do NOT exist. Access the key via `"key"` and nested properties via `"value.xxx"` (e.g. `"value.status"`, NOT `"status"`). CONFLICT PREEMPTION: if the user prompt references original field names, those names have been transformed away. Using them as col.field will produce runtime undefined. Always remap to `"key"` / `"value"` / `"value.xxx"`.
To display array fields as a single text cell in a Table, use @Join(array, separator). Do NOT use .join() or .toString().

Do NOT multiply values by 100 for display. Data fields named with "percent"/"Percent" (e.g. inputBandwidthPercent, cpuUsagePercent) already provide values in final percentage scale (e.g. 12.2323 means 12.2323%). Pass these values directly to Series, TextContent, Table cells, and all other components — multiplying by 100 produces incorrect values.

builtins.name: Count
builtins.description: Returns array length

builtins.name: First
builtins.description: Returns first element of array

builtins.name: Last
builtins.description: Returns last element of array

builtins.name: Sum
builtins.description: Sum of numeric array

builtins.name: Avg
builtins.description: Average of numeric array

builtins.name: Min
builtins.description: Minimum value in array

builtins.name: Max
builtins.description: Maximum value in array

builtins.name: Sort
builtins.description: Sort array by field. Direction: "asc" (default) or "desc"

builtins.name: Filter
builtins.signature: Filter(array, field, operator: "==" | "!=" | ">" | "<" | ">=" | "<=" | "contains", value) -> filtered array
builtins.description: Filter array by field value

builtins.name: Flatten
builtins.description: Flatten a nested array one level. Best used with array pluck: @Flatten(data.groups.items) extracts the "items" field from each group (producing items[][]) then flattens to items[]. Returns [] for null and non-array input.

builtins.name: ObjectEntries
builtins.description: Convert a plain object map into ordered rows of {key, value}. Access the object key via "key" and the original value via "value" (e.g. "value.status"). Original field names are NOT available — always use "key" and "value.xxx". Returns [] for null, arrays, and unsupported inputs.

builtins.name: ObjectKeys
builtins.description: Return the ordered keys of a plain object map as a string array. Returns [] for null, arrays, and unsupported inputs.

builtins.name: ObjectValues
builtins.description: Return the ordered values of a plain object map as an array. Returns [] for null, arrays, and unsupported inputs.

builtins.name: Round
builtins.description: Round to N decimal places (default 0)

builtins.name: Abs
builtins.description: Absolute value

builtins.name: Floor
builtins.description: Round down to nearest integer

builtins.name: Ceil
builtins.description: Round up to nearest integer

builtins.name: Number
builtins.description: Convert a value to a number. Strings are parsed; booleans map to 0/1; invalid values return 0. For string-to-number conversion in chart Series, use @Number(value). @Number can handle decimals; do not use the unsupported parseFloat — use @Number instead.

builtins.name: Switch
builtins.description: Map an enum value to a display result via a cases object. Numeric values are coerced to strings for key lookup. Returns default (null if omitted) when no case matches.

builtins.name: FormatDate
builtins.description: Format a date-like value for TEXT display ONLY (Table cells, Descriptions, TextContent). `value` accepts a Unix timestamp in seconds OR milliseconds (auto-detected), an ISO 8601 string; also maps over arrays. `style` accepts "dateTime", "time", "relative", or "date" (date-only, use ONLY when time-of-day is irrelevant), defaults to "dateTime". ⚠️ NEVER use @FormatDate on Chart labels — pass raw timestamp arrays directly; charts auto-format timestamps (same-day → time, cross-day → date). Using @FormatDate on Chart labels produces pre-formatted strings and breaks time-axis formatting. ⚠️ HARD RULE — pass the RAW timestamp value directly; NEVER divide by 1000 (`v / 1000`) or multiply by 1000 (`v * 1000`) to "convert units" — the engine auto-detects seconds vs milliseconds (10-digit = seconds, 13-digit = milliseconds). Doing so turns valid timestamps into 1970 dates.
builtins.returnType: string[] when param(0) is array, else string

builtins.name: FormatBytes
builtins.description: Format a byte count into a compact SI string (KB, MB, GB). Returns "" for nullish input.

builtins.name: FormatNumber
builtins.description: Format a scalar number as a locale-aware display string. Uses the renderer locale by default and returns raw input for invalid values.

builtins.name: FormatPercent
builtins.description: Format a ratio such as 0.125 as a locale-aware percentage display string, with optional decimal precision and locale override.

builtins.name: FormatDuration
builtins.description: Format an elapsed duration into a compact display string. Input defaults to seconds and also supports explicit "ms" input.

builtins.name: MergeObject
builtins.description: Merge multiple objects into one. Later objects override earlier ones. Non-object arguments are skipped. Returns {} when no objects are provided. Useful with @Each to expand array rows with extra fields.

builtins.name: Join
builtins.description: Join array elements into a single string with an optional separator (default ", "). Each element is converted to a string; null/undefined elements are skipped. Returns "" for null, non-array, or empty input.

builtins.name: String
builtins.description: Convert a number or boolean to string. Returns empty string for other types.

builtins.name: Each
builtins.description: Evaluate template for each element. varName is the loop variable - use it ONLY inside the template expression (inline). Do NOT create a separate statement for the template.

builtins.name: Render
builtins.description: Create a deferred render template for prop values. Binder names are string literals and are only in scope inside the template body.
